title: Contract Prover: runtime adapter and exhaustive backward-compat probes for API version transitions
creator: Anika Shah
description: Build a lightweight "contract prover" component and a set of exhaustive backward-compatibility probes that verify end-to-end API behavior across versions. The prover operates at two levels: (1) a runtime adapter that intercepts outgoing responses and asserts they conform to the active contract matrix (streaming envelopes, toolcall handshake, structured JSON schemas, and behavior flag semantics), and (2) an offline probe harness that runs shadow/dual requests plus randomized mutation tests against new model variants and flag combinations. The goal is to be able to safely roll runtime changes and deprecations with automated, measurable guarantees and clear failure signals for rollbacks.
background: We have repeated incidents where subtle streaming envelope changes or tool-calling handshake tweaks caused downstream SDKs and customer integrations to break during rollouts. Existing testbeds primarily focus on unit-level schema checks but do not exercise time-ordered streaming behavior, partial tool-call failures, or mixed flag matrices. This ticket creates an integrated prover + probe suite to surface these regressions earlier in CI and during canaries.
proposal: 1) Implement a thin runtime adapter that can be enabled via behavior flag (runtime.contract_prover=on). It records request/response traces and performs live assertions against a contract matrix that includes: message framing rules for streaming, required/optional fields for structured outputs, allowed toolcall error semantics, and expected tokenization/continuation patterns for chunked responses. 2) Build a probe harness that performs: shadow runs (dual-sends to old/new variants), fuzzed streaming (out-of-order and truncated chunks), and flag-space combinatorics sampling for the most risky flags. 3) Integrate prover signals into the Console as a dedicated "contract-prover" dashboard with failure reason categories and suggested rollback actions.
technical_design: - Runtime Adapter: middleware layer in serving runtime that attaches to the request pipeline. Lightweight assertions implemented as rule sets (regex, schema, sequence checks) and a pluggable hook to run more expensive heuristics in background. Assertions return either pass/warn/fail. Failures emit structured events to tracing and to a new metrics stream (contract_prover.violation_count).
rollout_plan: - Stage 1 (canary): enable adapter in read-only mode (flag=prover.mode=monitor) for 5% of traffic in dedicated cluster; collect violations for one week. - Stage 2 (shadow): enable probe harness in CI and dedicated smoke lanes to run dual requests against new model variants + flag permutations. - Stage 3 (enforce opt-in): switch to fail-on-violation for internal routes only; block runtime-deploys with > X violations/day. - Stage 4 (public rollout): notify customers and flip enforcement using holdback lists and grace periods per release.
test_plan: - Unit: rule engine tests for streaming envelope patterns and schema conformance. - Integration: shadow-run comparisons for a representative set of SDK calls (chat/stream, tool-call, structured output). - Fuzz: stream-chunk mutation harness that injects latency, truncation, and chunk-loss; validate adapter recovers or flags. - Regression: create a small corpus of historical incidents encoded as probes to ensure future changes do not reintroduce known breakages.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime adapter exists and can be toggled via behavior flag with monitor/enforce modes.
Probe harness can run shadow comparisons with a configurable set of flag permutations.
Prover emits structured violation events to tracing and metrics; Console dashboard renders top violation categories.
CI gates can run the probe harness and fail builds on configurable thresholds.
Runbook created for interpreting prover failures and recommended rollback steps.
out_of_scope: Full SDK-side adapters, customer-facing breaking-change notifications, and automatic code migrations for client libraries. Those will be separate follow-ups.
open_questions: What should be the default sampling strategy for the flag combinatorics? Exhaustive is expensive — prefer risk-ranked sampling.
Threshold for CI gating: how many violations per 1000 shadowed requests should fail the build?
Do we allow prover to auto-rollback a canary, or only alert and block manual promotion?
notes: - Coordinate with Observability guild to ensure contract_prover.violation_count is tagged by route, model, flag-set, and region. - Start with a compact initial contract matrix (stream framing + toolcall handshake + top-10 structured fields) and iterate based on violation telemetry.
